subject: math
title: Numbers to 1 000 000: Place Value, Comparing and Rounding
seo_title: Grade 5 Numbers to 1 000 000 Math Worksheets: Free, with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on numbers to 1 000 000 for the BC curriculum: place value, the value of each digit, expanded form, comparing and ordering, and rounding with real BC numbers. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The place of a digit tells you its value. The 4 in 453 000 is worth 400 000.
key_sub: Write three digits after each space: forty thousand five hundred three is 40 503, not 4503. To compare, count the digits first, then compare from the left.
body_html:
Place value to one million

Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. Ten hundred thousands make 1 000 000 (one million). Big numbers are split into groups of three digits. In BC we leave a small space between the groups (405 030), not a comma. A 4-digit number has no space (4503).

Place value disks show the same thing. Find the value of each group, then add.

Words to digits

Write forty thousand five hundred three in digits.

Forty thousand → 40. Five hundred three → 503 (always three digits after the space).

Answer: 40 503 (not 4503)

The value of a digit

The digit is the symbol. Its value depends on its place. In 471 250 the digit 7 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 70 000, not 7.

Expanded form and decomposing

Expanded form shows the value of each digit: 683 725 = 600 000 + 80 000 + 3000 + 700 + 20 + 5. Leave out the zeros: 405 030 = 400 000 + 5000 + 30.

Decompose

Write 453 000 in three ways.

Expanded form: 400 000 + 50 000 + 3000. It is also 45 ten thousands and 3 thousands, or 453 thousands.

Answer: 400 000 + 50 000 + 3000 = 45 ten thousands + 3 thousands = 453 thousands

Compare and order

First count the digits: a 6-digit number is greater than any 5-digit number. If both have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left until two digits are different.

Compare

634 050 ☐ 634 500

Hundred thousands: 6 = 6. Ten thousands: 3 = 3. Thousands: 4 = 4. Hundreds: 0 < 5.

Answer: 634 050 < 634 500

Number lines and rounding

On a number line, work out the size of each space first. To round, look at the digit one place to the right: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down.

Round 678 500 to the nearest …Look atAnswer
hundred thousandthe ten thousands digit: 7700 000
ten thousandthe thousands digit: 8680 000
thousandthe hundreds digit: 5679 000

Big numbers in BC

We see numbers to 1 000 000 in the populations of BC cities, in salmon counts on our rivers, in crowds at BC Place and in money raised for the Terry Fox Run. News reports often round them: Surrey’s 568 322 people in the 2021 Census becomes “about 570 000 people”.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out a zero (forty thousand five hundred three → 4503)Write three digits after the space: 40 | 503 → 40 503
Giving the digit, not its value (the 7 in 471 250 is 7)It is in the ten thousands place: 70 000
Counting the disks (3 + 4 + 2 = 9)Add the values: 300 000 + 40 000 + 200 = 340 200
Comparing the first digits only (98 765 > 102 345)Count the digits first: 102 345 > 98 765
Thinking every space on a number line is 1000Work out the space first: 400 000 to 500 000 in 10 spaces is 10 000 each
Rounding twice (345 120 → 350 000 → 400 000)Round the number you started with: 300 000

faq.q: What number concepts are in the BC Grade 5 math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 5 students in BC work with number concepts to 1 000 000: reading and writing numbers, place value, expanded form, comparing and ordering, and rounding. They also work with decimals to thousandths.

faq.q: How do you write one million in numbers?
faq.a: One million is 1 000 000: a 1 followed by six zeros, with a space between each group of three digits. It is 10 hundred thousands, or 1000 thousands.

faq.q: How do you write forty thousand five hundred three in numbers?
faq.a: Write 40 for the thousands part and 503 for the rest: 40 503. The part after the space always has three digits, so the number is not 4503.

faq.q: How do you round a 6-digit number to the nearest ten thousand?
faq.a: Look at the thousands digit. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, keep the ten thousands digit and change the rest to 0. So 568 322 rounds to 570 000 and 453 600 rounds to 450 000.

items.q: What number do the place value disks show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 3 × 100 000 = 300 000; 4 × 10 000 = 40 000; 2 × 100 = 200. Add them: 340 200. There are no thousands or tens or ones, so write 0 in those places. Do not just count the disks: each disk has its own value.

items.q: What number do the place value disks show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 2 × 100 000 = 200 000; 5 × 1000 = 5000; 1 × 10 = 10. Add them: 205 010. There are no ten thousands or hundreds or ones, so write 0 in those places. Do not just count the disks: each disk has its own value.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 635 274 the red 6 is in the hundred thousands place.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 428 916 the red 2 is in the ten thousands place.

items.q: In 743 816, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: In 743 816: hundred thousands 7, ten thousands 4, thousands 3, hundreds 8, tens 1, ones 6. The ten thousands digit is 4.

items.q: Which number is forty thousand five hundred three?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: forty thousand → 40. Then write the rest with three digits: five hundred three → 503. So the number is 40 503. 4503 leaves out the 0 in the thousands place.

items.q: Which number is three hundred six thousand forty?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: three hundred six thousand → 306. Then write the rest with three digits: forty → 040. So the number is 306 040.

items.q: What number do the place value disks show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 1 × 100 000 = 100 000; 3 × 10 000 = 30 000; 4 × 10 = 40; 2 × 1 = 2. Add them: 130 042. There are no thousands or hundreds, so write 0 in those places. Do not just count the disks: each disk has its own value.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 750 382 the red 0 is in the thousands place.

items.q: How do you write 604 050 in words?
c: six hundred four thousand five hundred
items.e: Split 604 050 into the thousands part and the rest: 604 thousand and 50. Say each part: six hundred four thousand fifty.

items.q: Which number is five hundred twenty thousand seven?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: five hundred twenty thousand → 520. Then write the rest with three digits: seven → 007. So the number is 520 007.

items.q: In 590 264, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: In 590 264: hundred thousands 5, ten thousands 9, thousands 0, hundreds 2, tens 6, ones 4. The thousands digit is 0. The 0 shows there are no thousands.

items.q: How many hundred thousands make 1 000 000?
items.e: Count by hundred thousands: 100 000, 200 000 … 1 000 000. That is 10 hundred thousands. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

items.q: What number do the place value disks show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 4 × 100 000 = 400 000; 6 × 100 = 600; 3 × 1 = 3. Add them: 400 603. There are no ten thousands or thousands or tens, so write 0 in those places. Do not just count the disks: each disk has its own value.

items.q: Which number is eight hundred fifteen thousand four hundred?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: eight hundred fifteen thousand → 815. Then write the rest with three digits: four hundred → 400. So the number is 815 400. Fifteen is 15, not 50.

items.q: How do you write 218 070 in words?
c: two hundred eighteen thousand seven hundred
items.e: Split 218 070 into the thousands part and the rest: 218 thousand and 70. Say each part: two hundred eighteen thousand seventy. Eighteen is 18, eighty is 80.

items.q: Ten groups of 100 000 make what number?
items.e: 10 × 100 000 = 1 000 000. Count by hundred thousands: 100 000, 200 000 … 1 000 000. Ten hundred thousands make one million.

items.q: Which number is one million?
items.e: One million is 1000 thousands. Write 1, then two groups of three zeros: 1 000 000. It has 7 digits. (100 000 is one hundred thousand.)

items.q: How do you write 470 012 in words?
c: four hundred seventy thousand one hundred twenty
items.e: Split 470 012 into the thousands part and the rest: 470 thousand and 12. Say each part: four hundred seventy thousand twelve.

items.q: What number is 1 more than 999 999?
items.e: 999 999 + 1: every 9 becomes 0 as you regroup, and a 1 goes in the millions place: 1 000 000. (999 998 is 1 less.)

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 5 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 5 hundred thousands = 500 000. The digit is 5, but its value is 500 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 7 ten thousands = 70 000. The digit is 7, but its value is 70 000.

items.q: What is the value of the 7 in 471 250?
items.e: The 7 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 7 ten thousands = 70 000. The digit is 7, but its value is 70 000.

items.q: What is the value of the 3 in 236 091?
items.e: The 3 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 3 ten thousands = 30 000. The digit is 3, but its value is 30 000.

items.q: In the 2021 Census, Kelowna had 144 576 people. What is the value of the 5?
items.e: 144 576 is 1 hundred thousand, 4 ten thousands, 4 thousands, 5 hundreds, 7 tens and 6 ones. The 5 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 500.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 6 hundreds = 600. The digit is 6, but its value is 600.

items.q: What is the value of the 8 in 702 846?
items.e: The 8 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 8 hundreds = 800. The digit is 8, but its value is 800.

items.q: Which number has a 6 in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: 632 054 has 6 hundred thousands, 3 ten thousands, 2 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens, 4 ones. The hundred thousands digit is 6.

items.q: Which number has 0 ten thousands?
items.e: 708 516 is 7 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 8 thousands, 5 hundreds, 1 ten and 6 ones. The other numbers have 8 or 7 ten thousands.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 8 tens = 80. The digit is 8, but its value is 80.

items.q: What is the value of the 9 in 915 384?
items.e: The 9 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 9 hundred thousands = 900 000. The digit is 9, but its value is 900 000.

items.q: Which number has a 4 in the thousands place?
items.e: 274 019 has 2 hundred thousands, 7 ten thousands, 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 1 ten, 9 ones. The thousands digit is 4.

items.q: 478 300 = ☐ thousands and 3 hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 478 300 = 478 000 + 300. 478 000 is 478 thousands. So 478 300 = 478 thousands and 3 hundreds. (8 is only the thousands digit.)

items.q: In 903 407, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 903 407 is 9 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. The tens digit is 0: there are no tens.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 5 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 5 thousands = 5000. The digit is 5, but its value is 5000.

items.q: What is the value of the 2 in 468 205?
items.e: The 2 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 2 hundreds = 200. The digit is 2, but its value is 200.

items.q: Which number has a 0 in the ten thousands place?
items.e: 508 371 has 5 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 8 thousands, 3 hundreds, 7 tens, 1 one. The ten thousands digit is 0.

items.q: 260 000 = ☐ ten thousands. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 100 000 = 10 ten thousands, so 260 000 = 20 + 6 = 26 ten thousands. Check: 26 × 10 000 = 260 000.

items.q: The 3 in 300 000 is worth how many times the 3 in 30 000?
items.e: The first 3 is worth 300 000. The second 3 is worth 30 000. 300 000 ÷ 30 000 = 10. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. (270 000 is the difference, not how many times.)

items.q: In 550 000, the first 5 is worth how many times the second 5?
items.e: The first 5 is in the hundred thousands place: 500 000. The second 5 is in the ten thousands place: 50 000. 500 000 ÷ 50 000 = 10.

items.q: What is 683 725 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: hundred thousands 6 = 600 000, ten thousands 8 = 80 000, thousands 3 = 3000, hundreds 7 = 700, tens 2 = 20, ones 5 = 5. That is 600 000 + 80 000 + 3000 + 700 + 20 + 5.

items.q: What is 453 000 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: hundred thousands 4 = 400 000, ten thousands 5 = 50 000, thousands 3 = 3000. That is 400 000 + 50 000 + 3000. A 0 adds nothing, so it is left out.

items.q: What number is 800 000 + 600 + 4?
items.e: Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place. 800 000 + 600 + 4 → 800 604.

items.q: What number is 300 000 + 70 000 + 20?
items.e: Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place. 300 000 + 70 000 + 20 → 370 020.

items.q: 600 000 + ☐ + 7000 + 200 + 5 = 687 205. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 687 205 has 8 in the ten thousands place. That is worth 80 000.

items.q: ☐ + 30 000 + 40 + 2 = 530 042. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 530 042 has 5 in the hundred thousands place. That is worth 500 000.

items.q: What is 405 030 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: hundred thousands 4 = 400 000, thousands 5 = 5000, tens 3 = 30. That is 400 000 + 5000 + 30. A 0 adds nothing, so it is left out.

items.q: What number is 500 000 + 9?
items.e: Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place. 500 000 + 9 → 500 009.

items.q: 700 000 + 4000 + ☐ = 704 009. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 704 009 has 9 in the ones place. That is worth 9.

items.q: What is 720 080 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: hundred thousands 7 = 700 000, ten thousands 2 = 20 000, tens 8 = 80. That is 700 000 + 20 000 + 80. A 0 adds nothing, so it is left out.
The parts are not in order. Sort them from the greatest place: 200 000 + 40 000 + 3000 + 60 + 1 = 243 061. Do not write the digits in the order you see them.

items.q: 100 000 + 50 000 + ☐ + 6 = 150 086. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 150 086 has 8 in the tens place. That is worth 80.

items.q: What is 930 016 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: hundred thousands 9 = 900 000, ten thousands 3 = 30 000, tens 1 = 10, ones 6 = 6. That is 900 000 + 30 000 + 10 + 6. A 0 adds nothing, so it is left out.
Work out each part: 9 × 100 000 = 900 000, 6 × 1000 = 6000, 5 × 10 = 50. Add them: 906 050. Write 0 in every empty place.

items.q: 453 000 = ☐ thousands. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 453 000 = 453 groups of 1000, so it is 453 thousands. Check: 453 × 1000 = 453 000.
Work out each part: 7 × 100 000 = 700 000, 2 × 10 = 20, 9 × 1 = 9. Add them: 700 029. Write 0 in every empty place.

items.q: What number is 3 hundred thousands, 14 ten thousands and 2 thousands?
items.e: 3 hundred thousands = 300 000 and 14 ten thousands = 140 000. 300 000 + 140 000 + 2000 = 442 000. Do not write 14 inside the number: 14 ten thousands is 1 hundred thousand and 4 ten thousands.

items.q: 260 400 = 1 hundred thousand, ☐ ten thousands and 4 hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 260 400 = 2 hundred thousands, 6 ten thousands and 4 hundreds. Trade 1 hundred thousand for 10 ten thousands: 10 + 6 = 16 ten thousands. Check: 100 000 + 160 000 + 400 = 260 400.

items.q: Which is another way to make 527 000?
c: 4 hundred thousands, 2 ten thousands and 7 thousands
5 hundred thousands, 12 ten thousands and 7 thousands
4 hundred thousands, 12 ten thousands and 7 thousands
4 hundred thousands, 12 ten thousands and 70 thousands
items.e: 4 hundred thousands = 400 000 and 12 ten thousands = 120 000. 400 000 + 120 000 + 7000 = 527 000. (The others make 427 000, 627 000 and 590 000.)

items.q: Which is not equal to 320 000?
items.e: 3 hundred thousands and 2 thousands = 300 000 + 2000 = 302 000, not 320 000. 32 ten thousands = 320 000, 320 thousands = 320 000 and 200 000 + 120 000 = 320 000.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 3 thousands is more than 0 thousands. So 453 000 > 450 300.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 102 345 has 6 digits and 98 765 has only 5, so 102 345 is greater. A big first digit does not matter when a number has fewer digits.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 5 thousands is more than 2 thousands. So 365 120 > 362 150. 365 120 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 89 999 has only 5 digits, so it is the least, even though it starts with 8. Every 6-digit number is at least 100 000.

items.q: Put 453 000, 435 000, 450 300 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 4 hundred thousands. Ten thousands: 3 < 5, so 435 000 is the least. 453 000 and 450 300 both have 5 ten thousands. Thousands: 0 < 3, so 450 300 < 453 000. Order: 435 000, 450 300, 453 000.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 5 hundreds is more than 0 hundreds. So 634 500 > 634 050.

items.q: Which number is between 450 000 and 460 000?
items.e: A number between 450 000 and 460 000 has 4 hundred thousands and 5 ten thousands. 458 700 fits. 465 000 is too big, 449 900 is too small and 45 870 has only 5 digits.

items.q: Use each of the digits 7, 2, 9, 4, 1 and 6 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the hundred thousands place, then the next biggest, and so on: 9, 7, 6, 4, 2, 1. The greatest number is 976 421.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 79 890 has only 5 digits, so it is the least. For the 6-digit numbers, compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 9 hundreds is more than 0 hundreds. So 708 900 > 708 090. 708 900 is the greatest.

items.q: Put 612 040, 164 020, 621 040 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: Hundred thousands: 1 < 6, so 164 020 is the least. 612 040 and 621 040 both have 6 hundred thousands. Ten thousands: 2 > 1, so 621 040 > 612 040. Order: 621 040, 612 040, 164 020.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. Start with the hundred thousands: 8 hundred thousands is more than 7 hundred thousands. So 800 091 > 799 999.

items.q: Which number is between 799 000 and 801 000?
items.e: 800 150 is more than 800 000 and less than 801 000, so it is between 799 000 and 801 000. 801 500 is too big, 790 900 is too small and 80 015 has only 5 digits.

items.q: Use each of the digits 5, 0, 8, 3, 6 and 1 once. What is the least 6-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 6-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smallest other digit first: 1. Then 0, 3, 5, 6, 8: 103 568. (013 568 is just 13 568, which has only 5 digits.)

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 6 hundreds is more than 0 hundreds. So 425 600 > 425 060. 425 060 is the least.

items.q: Put 99 500, 105 000, 100 500, 95 050 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: The 5-digit numbers are less than the 6-digit numbers. 95 050 < 99 500 (thousands: 5 < 9). 100 500 < 105 000 (thousands: 0 < 5). Order: 95 050, 99 500, 100 500, 105 000.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 8 hundreds is more than 2 hundreds. So 517 824 > 517 284.

items.q: 38☐ 400 > 386 500. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred thousands and ten thousands are the same. Compare the thousands: the box must be 6 or more. If it is 6, compare the hundreds: 4 < 5, so 386 400 is too small. 388 400 > 386 500.

items.q: Use each of the digits 6, 0, 2, 0, 9 and 5 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Biggest digit first: 9, then 6, then 5, then 2. The two 0s go last, in the tens and ones places: 965 200.

items.q: Put 990 000, 1 000 000, 909 999, 999 000 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 1 000 000 has 7 digits, so it is the greatest. Then compare the 6-digit numbers: 999 000 > 990 000 (thousands: 9 > 0) and 990 000 > 909 999 (ten thousands: 9 > 0). Order: 1 000 000, 999 000, 990 000, 909 999.

items.q: 625 ☐80 < 625 450. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The first three digits are the same. Compare the hundreds: the box must be 4 or less. If it is 4, compare the tens: 8 > 5, so 625 480 is too big. 625 380 < 625 450.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1 000 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 100 000. The arrow is 2 spaces after 500 000: 600 000, 700 000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 400 000 to 500 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 10 000, not 1000. The arrow is 3 spaces after 400 000: 430 000.

items.q: Round 453 600 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Nearest ten thousand: 453 600 is between 450 000 and 460 000. Look at the thousands digit: 3. 4 or less, so round down. So 453 600 rounds to 450 000.

items.q: Round 678 500 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Nearest thousand: 678 500 is between 678 000 and 679 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up. So 678 500 rounds to 679 000. Do not just drop the hundreds: 678 000 is cutting off, not rounding.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 200 000 to 300 000 there are only 5 equal spaces, so each space is 100 000 ÷ 5 = 20 000. The arrow is 3 spaces after 200 000: 220 000, 240 000, 260 000. (230 000 counts each space as 10 000.)

items.q: Round 345 120 to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: Nearest hundred thousand: 345 120 is between 300 000 and 400 000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. So 345 120 rounds to 300 000. Round the number you started with. Do not round to 350 000 first and then to 400 000.

items.q: Round 850 960 to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: Nearest hundred thousand: 850 960 is between 800 000 and 900 000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up. So 850 960 rounds to 900 000.

items.q: Round 299 610 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Nearest thousand: 299 610 is between 299 000 and 300 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up. So 299 610 rounds to 300 000. 299 thousands + 1 thousand = 300 thousands, so the answer is 300 000.

items.q: In the 2021 Census, Surrey had 568 322 people. Round this number to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Nearest ten thousand: 568 322 is between 560 000 and 570 000. Look at the thousands digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up. So 568 322 rounds to 570 000.

items.q: In the 2021 Census, Kamloops had 97 902 people and Nanaimo had 99 863 people. Which city had more people?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 9 thousands is more than 7 thousands. So 99 863 > 97 902. Nanaimo had more people.

items.q: In the 2021 Census, Kelowna had 144 576 people, Abbotsford had 153 524 and Coquitlam had 148 625. Which list goes from least to greatest?
items.e: Ten thousands: 4 < 5, so 153 524 is the greatest. 144 576 and 148 625 both have 4 ten thousands. Thousands: 4 < 8, so 144 576 < 148 625. Order: 144 576, 148 625, 153 524.

items.q: Volunteers counted three hundred forty thousand five hundred sockeye salmon swimming up a BC river. Write the number in digits.
items.e: Say the thousands part first: three hundred forty thousand → 340. Then write the rest with three digits: five hundred → 500. So the number is 340 500. 34 500 leaves out the 0 in the thousands place.

items.q: In the 2021 Census, Burnaby had 249 125 people. What is the value of the 4?
items.e: 249 125 is 2 hundred thousands, 4 ten thousands, 9 thousands, 1 hundred, 2 tens and 5 ones. The 4 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 40 000, not 4.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the number of people at a sold-out football game at BC Place in Vancouver?
items.e: BC Place is a stadium that holds about 54 000 people, so about 54 000 is a good estimate. About 540 or 5400 is far too few, and 540 000 is almost as many people as live in Surrey.

items.q: A BC city’s population, rounded to the nearest hundred thousand, is 200 000. Which could be the real population?
items.e: Numbers from 150 000 up to 249 999 round to 200 000. 209 937 has 0 ten thousands, so it rounds down to 200 000. 250 000 rounds up to 300 000, 149 900 rounds to 100 000, and 20 990 is far too small. (209 937 was the population of Richmond in the 2021 Census.)

items.q: A fish counter on a river counted 386 452 pink salmon in one season. Round the count to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Nearest thousand: 386 452 is between 386 000 and 387 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. So 386 452 rounds to 386 000.

items.q: Schools in a BC school district raised one hundred five thousand three hundred dollars for the Terry Fox Run. Write the amount in numbers.
items.e: Say the thousands part first: one hundred five thousand → 105. Then write the rest with three digits: three hundred → 300. So the number is 105 300. The amount is $105 300.

items.q: A region had 589 650 people. Twenty years later it has 100 000 more people. How many people live there now?
items.e: Adding 100 000 changes the hundred thousands digit: 5 + 1 = 6 hundred thousands. 589 650 + 100 000 = 689 650. (599 650 adds only 10 000.)

items.q: Emma’s mystery number has 7 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 2 tens and 0 ones. What is it?
items.e: Write one digit for each place, with 0 for the empty places: 7, 0, 4, 0, 2, 0. That is 704 020.

items.q: A salmon hatchery on Vancouver Island releases 100 000 young coho salmon each spring. How many does it release in 6 springs?
